clue.text: Girl climber with black-eyes?

definitions.meaning: a girl's first name, as in a common female forename
the black-eyed vine Thunbergia, a climbing plant with dark-centred flowers, bears this name

explanation.surface: A girl who goes climbing has come home with two black eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Black-eyed Susan is a climbing plant with yellow flowers and dark centres; the question mark flags the punning plural 'black-eyes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female forename for a girl, and the second half of the plant name black-eyed Susan, a climbing vine.

clue.text: See miser hide at Welsh town

indicators.note: one piece sits next to the other, the hide word followed by the town

parts.note: skin is hide
Flint is a town in north Wales

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted man is seen hiding in a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Flint is a town in north-east Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a stingy person who hoards money, a mean hoarder.

clue.text: A plant like the Jerusalem artichoke can be fun in easier borders

definitions.text: A plant like the Jerusalem artichoke

indicators.note: the easier word borders, or surrounds, the rearranged letters

parts.note: slower means easier, as in an easier pace

indicators.note: fun can be something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant can be fun to grow along the edges of a gentler garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is the anagram signal and 'borders' the container; 'easier' means at a gentler pace. The Jerusalem artichoke is a species of Helianthus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem artichoke is Helianthus tuberosus, a tall yellow-flowered member of the same genus.

clue.text: Bellini's opera cut short? That is mean!

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini

explanation.surface: An opera by Bellini is shortened, and someone complains it is unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective meaning stingy, but it is the noun for an average.
explanation.definitionFit: The norm is the usual standard or average, as the mean is.

clue.text: Change dominates this part of Kent

indicators.note: an order to change tells us the letters of the next word must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something about money or alteration dominates life in a corner of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a noun meaning coins, but it is the anagram signal. Kent is a county in south-east England, and this town is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: The county town of Kent sits on the River Medway, a place within that English county.

clue.text: Antisocial sort, St Thomas, in rip-off!

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy loner is caught up in a scam at St Thomas's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip-off' looks like a swindle, but 'off' is the anagram signal for ST THOMAS IN RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dislikes and avoids other people, a hater of humankind.

clue.text: Slough outbuilding

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off, as a snake its skin

explanation.definitionFit: To cast off, as a snake does its skin, and a garden hut used for storage.

clue.text: Daisy is a neat looker!

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
an eye is what looks

explanation.surface: A girl named Daisy is said to be a tidy beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but it is an old word for cattle. 'Daisy' looks like a name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye is a large white-petalled wild daisy of meadows.

clue.text: Acclaim content of next Olympics

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what it holds, so the answer is found inside the words

explanation.surface: Praise is due for what the next Olympic Games will contain.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, as to acclaim is.

clue.text: Meal has no starter, here at "The Bull", we hear

indicators.note: with no starter, the meal word loses its first letter, its opening course in the surface

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: At a pub called The Bull, rumour says dinner comes without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bull' looks like a pub, but it is the bullseye on a dartboard; the ring around it is named by the answer, which is darts talk, hence 'we hear'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a dartboard the ring surrounding the bullseye is the inner ring, so a dart landing there is in that zone.

clue.text: But is it prepared by the bank-teller?

definitions.text: But is it prepared by the bank-teller?

parts.words: But is it prepared by the bank-teller?
parts.note: a teller tells, so a bank-teller might seem to make a spoken declaration; but a bank also prepares a summary of an account

explanation.definitionFit: A bank sends customers an account summary, and a teller in the sense of someone who tells makes a declaration.

clue.text: Commercial term evident as new?

indicators.note: making something new reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a commercial expression is plainly a fresh coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a TV advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial on television or radio is a paid promotion, an advert.

clue.text: Ferocious cut?

definitions.meaning: an old word for fierce or cruel

explanation.definitionFit: Fierce and savage in old usage ('one fell swoop'), and to chop down a tree with an axe.

clue.text: Jack reverses vehicle in outskirts of Kilbride

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, the reversed vehicle sitting within the outer letters
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so take the first and last letters of Kilbride
a vehicle that reverses goes backwards, so the word for it is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A man called Jack backs his van into the edge of the Scottish town of East Kilbride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name, but it is the playing card. 'reverses' turns the vehicle round, and 'in' places it within the outer letters of Kilbride.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the jack is also called the knave, the court card below the queen.

clue.text: Thriving in the spring

definitions.meaning: a spring of water from the ground, a source tapped for drinking

explanation.definitionFit: Healthy and flourishing, and a source of water drawn from underground, as a spring is.

clue.text: Swift attack to capture prince

indicators.note: to capture is to take hold, so the attack word surrounds the prince letter

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A quick assault is launched to seize a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means very quick, as swift does.

clue.text: Charge guinea for handles?

parts.note: a fee is a charge
a guinea was one pound and one shilling, abbreviated L for pound and S for shilling

explanation.surface: A fee of a guinea is charged for handles.
explanation.walkthrough: The guinea was an old British coin worth £1 1s; pounds and shillings were written L and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something is to touch and grope it with the fingers.

clue.text: Season before, defeated and tanned

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other in the answer, the season word first

parts.note: to season timber is to weather it, leaving it exposed to the air
beaten means defeated

explanation.surface: A team beaten in the season before comes back sunburnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a noun such as summer, but it is a verb: wood is seasoned, or weathered, by exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin darkened and toughened by long exposure to sun and wind is both tanned and worn by the elements.

clue.text: Testing can be wearisome, al fresco

parts.note: trying means wearisome or tiresome
al fresco means in the open air, outdoors

explanation.surface: Testing outdoors can be exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to sample it in practice, giving it a trial.

clue.text: The late shift?

parts.note: not a night work rota but a shift, a loose dress, worn late at night in bed

explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple loose dress, and one worn at night in bed is a sleeping garment.

clue.text: How army reserves perform, being one-all in the ground?

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the score going within the ground word

parts.note: territory is ground or land
one is the Roman numeral I, followed by the word all as written

explanation.surface: A reserve army team draws one-all at its home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was the British Army's volunteer reserve; its members serve in that capacity, hence the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's volunteer reserve was the Territorial Army, so reservists serve in a manner befitting that force.

clue.text: Mail has gone astray in the capital

indicators.note: post that has gone astray is lost and jumbled, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter has been lost in the post somewhere in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the capital' is a cryptic stretch: the answer is the capital of Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city and seat of government of Peru, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Night-climber of the wall in Paris

parts.note: le is French for the, taken from the Paris setting of the following words
mur is French for wall

explanation.surface: A nocturnal climber scales a wall in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' marks both words as French. Lemurs are tree-climbing primates of Madagascar, mostly active at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A Madagascan primate that climbs trees and is mostly active after dark.

clue.text: Red wine-try some, doctor?

indicators.note: to try some is to taste a part, so the answer is a small part found inside these words

explanation.surface: A doctor is offered a glass of red wine to taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a claret from the Bordeaux region, a red wine.

clue.text: Hot-rod no longer driven in shipyards?

definitions.text: Hot-rod no longer driven in shipyards?

parts.words: Hot-rod no longer driven in shipyards?
parts.note: not a souped-up car but a red-hot metal pin hammered through steel plates, a job largely replaced by welding in modern yards

explanation.definitionFit: A metal fastener heated and hammered through plates was used to join ships' hulls before welding took over.

clue.text: Granny King has no time to finish

indicators.note: to finish means at the end, so the time letter comes last

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An old king has no time left to finish his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granny' looks like a grandmother, but a granny is a kind of insecure reef-type tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny is a type of tie made in rope, like a reef but crossed the wrong way.

clue.text: Unpremeditated shot?

explanation.definitionFit: A snap decision is made on the spur of the moment, and a snapshot is a casual photograph.

clue.text: Tropical plant approved by artist

parts.note: OK means approved
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A tropical plant is given the thumbs-up by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a tropical plant grown for its edible green pods, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Paris work-girl finds little place to eat on motorway

indicators.note: one piece is placed on the other, the dining word following the road

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written MI in crosswords
a dinette is a small dining area

explanation.surface: A girl finds a small café on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a young Parisian shop assistant or seamstress, French for a working girl at midday.

clue.text: Kentucky too strange for a Japanese city

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

indicators.note: something strange is out of order, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor finds Kentucky too strange compared with Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' is the anagram signal for 'too'; 'for' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The former imperial capital of Japan, famous for its temples.

clue.text: Alpine music factory?

parts.note: rock is a kind of music
a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: A mountain-top factory turns out records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpine' looks like an adjective about the Alps, but it is a noun: a small plant grown in rockeries.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a small mountain plant grown in rock gardens.

clue.text: Bell one of the three from "The Parsonage"-here in London?

definitions.text: Bell one of the three from "The Parsonage"
definitions.meaning: the Brontë sisters of Haworth Parsonage wrote as Currer, Ellis and the third Bell, Anne's pen name

explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë published under a male pen name with the surname Bell, which is also a district in west London.
